thread:
Maya R: quick share — ran quantization sweep on orion-lite-11b across slices (slice-alpha). int8 / int6 / int4 results below, looking for product/GTN recommendation and rollout plan. TL;DR at the bottom.

Oliver T: paste the unit-econ numbers?

Maya R: sure — condensed: 
- int8: latency p95 180ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.95, quality baseline (anchor) = 0.0%
- int6: latency p95 160ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.57 (~40% savings), quality delta = -0.6% avg (narrowband), longform delta ~-0.6%
- int4: latency p95 150ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.36 (~62% savings), quality delta = -2.8% avg, longform delta ~-4.5%
- sample mix: 65% short chat, 25% multi-turn, 10% longform
- notes: int4 has failure mode on retrieval-heavy prompts (hallucination uptick)

Sanjay P: nice. marginal-token ROI looks good for int6. Quick rule of thumb I use: if quality drop <= 1% and cost savings >= 30% -> recommend as default for non-critical routes. int6 fits. int4 is tempting for pure short-chat but risk vs reward for multi-turn is sketchy.

Lucy K: product question: for GTN/consumer chat, is int6 perceptibly different for users? any metrics on subtle quality regressions?

Maya R: subjective check: human eval on top-150 samples shows ~95% of int6 responses indistinguishable from int8. Regression clusters: rare factual precision in long context and longer reasoning chains. We instrumented a small pass/fail: 
```
- automated QA exact-match drop: int6 -0.7%, int4 -3.2%
- rerank delta (MRR): int6 -0.4%, int4 -2.9%
```

EvalBot: smoke tests finished: QA-suite(1000 cases): int6 pass rate 98.6% (~anchor 99.2%), int4 pass rate 96.1%. Latency SLOs fine.

Oliver T: product ops-wise, I'd run canary: 5% traffic int6 default for 48h, watch these signals: 
- GTN metrics: usage retention, replies-per-session, complaint rate
- infra: P95 latency, OOM/eviction rates
- eval slices: top-20 customer prompts, retrieval-heavy slices

Sanjay P: routing suggestion: hybrid by length + slice flags. Pseudo-config: 
```
route_rules:
  - if customer_slice in [longform, enterprise]: model_variant: int8
  - elif token_length > 256: model_variant: int8
  - elif prompt_tag == "short-burst": model_variant: int4 (opt-in)
  - else: model_variant: int6
traffic_split(canary): {int6: 5%, int8: 95%}
```
We should also enable KV-prefix caching for short bursts to further lower cost.

Lucy K: ok — product preference is conservative. We want int6 as an opt-out default for consumer tiers, but enterprise/SLAs remain int8. For GTN comms: message should emphasize latency/cost wins and the small measured regressions + rollback plan.

Maya R: I'll draft the rollout PR + GTN blurb. Proposed rollout checklist: 
1) Canary 5% x 48h with slice monitors 
2) Run synthetic replay on top-20 customers (24h) 
3) If no signal regression, ramp to 50% over 7 days 
4) After 14 days, evaluate retention/quality windows and finalize default mapping

Oliver T: +1. add an automated guard: if any of these spike beyond threshold -> auto-fallback to int8 for affected customer_slice: 
- complaint_rate +0.2pp or 
- QA-suite delta >1.5% on monitored slices

Sanjay P: scorecard fields we should attach to the PR: unit-cost numbers, p95 latency, human-eval pass rate, rerank MRR delta, top-10 failure examples, rollback steps. Thresholds: fail if human-eval drop >1.2% or rerank MRR delta >1.0%.

Maya R: TL;DR recommendation: make int6 the default for consumer chat (opt-out), keep int8 for longform/enterprise, offer int4 as an opt-in experimental route for pure short-burst flows behind a feature flag. Canary + automatic guard rails required. I'll tag @Lucy K for signoff on GTN copy and @Sanjay P for ops checklist. :rocket:

Lucy K: thanks — please ping me when PR is ready. I'm ok to signoff on the messaging if the canary dashboard includes the top-5 customer slices. :thumbsup:

Maya R: will do — draft incoming in ~2 hours.
